$comment: One price schedule — GitHub issue #366, DECISIONS.md § D525 clause 2, docs/38 § 2.1. Every price a player pays for a change, in one place, so the same change costs the same in Scenario, in Career and in the fix-a-building editor. The figures are DRAFTED, not measured: a price is game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's. Where two shipped lists already agreed the agreed figure is kept and said so; where they disagreed the disagreement is recorded in the entry's note. See packages/viz/src/pricing/parse.ts. GitHub issue #467 (DECISIONS.md § D535) added two things. Six new rows and three paths added to dispatch-rules, at no change to its price, price the twenty-two dials the scenarios used to offer for nothing, and every note that carries them is an AGENT'S PROPOSAL, APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11, saying field by field what is MEASURED (nothing about the figure), what is DERIVED (the ceiling the shipped opening budgets and stage hints put on it) and what is CHOSEN. And a `withheld` block names what no scenario sells at any price, by the product owner's own ruling: not for sale is a different answer from priced high, so it is a list of paths and a note rather than a row carrying a large number.

tiers.name: Dispatcher
tiers.note: How the cars are told to behave. Nothing is installed and nothing is cut, so it is the cheap end of the ladder and tuning is nearly free.

tiers.name: Equipment
tiers.note: Settings and fittings on kit the building already has — door timings, sensors, landing panels. Dearer than telling the cars what to do, cheaper than changing the building. THE TYPICAL IS DERIVED, NEVER CHOSEN (packages/viz/src/pricing/parse.ts#violationsIn): it is this tier's own median of the price on each row's face, a flat row's price and a rated row's per-unit rate. It read 9 until GitHub issue #437 added the 1 u per-landing landing-panels row, which moved the fifteen-value median down to 6. That is arithmetic rather than a re-pricing -- no shipped row's price moved -- and the ladder still ascends: 2 u, 6 u, 20 u.

tiers.name: Building
tiers.note: The fabric: a new shaft or car, a faster or larger machine, a rezoned bank, a moved floor. The dearest end, and the only one that books long works.

changes.name: Where idle cars wait
changes.note: Free in every shipped list. Four fix cases price the idle strategy at 0 units and none prices it higher.

changes.name: How calls are assigned
changes.note: The fix cases price an assignment-mode change at 2 units as a diagnosis and at 8 as a costly fix. 2 is taken: the 8 was a case where the same press also bought a split threshold, which is priced on its own row now. GitHub issue #467 WIDENED WHAT THIS ROW COVERS AND DID NOT MOVE ITS PRICE: the three eligibility filters, the direction-reversal constraint and the sole-car bypass guard were free in every scenario that offered them, and they are bought here now. AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the product owner to accept, tighten or reject under the 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values, and priced rather than withheld by the owner's 2026-09-10 ruling on that issue (DECISIONS.md § D535). APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. MEASURED: nothing about the figure, which is this row's unchanged 2 u; what is measured is only that buying this row reaches a run (packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts). DERIVED: that these five dials cannot sit on a row of their own. Stages 9 and 10 open on 15 u and suggest constraints.noDirectionReversal and answer.allowBypassIfSoleEligibleCar respectively beside dispatch.assignmentMode, weights.starvation and a landing-panel lever at 13 u, and packages/viz/src/campaign/parse.ts prices a stage's suggested levers together at its opening rung — measured by the loader on the first draft of this issue, which priced them on two 2 u rows of their own and was refused at 17 u against 15 on both stages. CHOSEN: this row rather than re-authoring two stages' hints or their opening rule, because the dials are part of the same act this row already sells — core declares the eligibility filters and the hard constraint in the stage of its dispatch pipeline that decides which cars a call may go to, and its own descriptions name opposite-direction pickup and no direction reversal as the two halves of conventional collective behaviour — and because the bypass guard is a starvation rule, as weights.starvation beside it is. Covered as groups where core groups them, so an eligibility filter or a hard constraint core declares tomorrow is priced here with no edit. FOR THE OWNER: the hints on stage-2-morning-rush, stage-7-prove-it, stage-8-the-headline-address, stage-10-the-bed-and-the-visitor and brief-e5-handling-capacity name answer.allowBypassIfSoleEligibleCar, a dial this row now sells, and on each of those scenarios moving it alone leaves every replication of both seed sets unchanged, so following that hint now costs 2 u for an unchanged run; packages/viz/src/scenario/pricedRowsReachTheRun.test.ts measures this and holds it in both directions as HINTS_THAT_DO_NOT_MOVE_THE_RUN, which an entry leaves only on the commit that makes its move change a replication.

changes.name: Destination panels, per landing
changes.note: GitHub issue #437 stage 2, DECISIONS.md section D619. THE FIRST RATED ROW ON THIS SCHEDULE -- issue #478 / section D552 built the rate-times-quantity seam and named this change as the row that would use it. Al-Kodmany (Buildings 2015, 5(3), 1070-1104) section 2.2.1 is the premise: destination panels are installed on all floors (full configuration) or only on the busiest ones (hybrid configuration), so panel count is a quantity a building has rather than a switch it is on one side of. PROVENANCE, per the product owner's 2026-09-08 standing ruling on governed data/ values: THIS FIGURE IS AN AGENT'S PROPOSAL, drafted for the owner to accept, tighten or reject. What is MEASURED: nothing about the price. packages/experiments/src/benchmark/landingPanelDeployment.ts measures what panels are WORTH on midtown-office at n=200 under common random numbers -- entrance-only is bit-identical to a full deployment under a pure up-peak and 1.294 s of time-to-destination short of it under a mixed day -- and a worth is not a cost. What is DERIVED: the bracket. Two shipped rows already price a whole-building destination install, destination-panels at 13 u and full-destination at 24 u, and midtown-office, the building #437 names, has 21 landings; 1 u per landing puts a full deployment there at 21 u, between the two. What is CHOSEN: 1 rather than 2, and a landing rather than a floor group as the unit. THE CEILING IS A CEILING AND NOT A PRICE: 165 is the landing count of the largest shipped building (burj-class-reference), so that the schedule ceiling scenario/budget.ts derives -- every change bought at once, a rated row at its declared most -- stays true of every building the game ships; packages/viz/src/pricing/rate.test.ts derives that number from data/buildings/ through the loader rather than trusting this one. THIS ROW DOES NOT REPLACE destination-panels, and the two do not overlap by path: that row prices switching the DISPATCHER into destination mode (dispatcher.dispatch.callType and .passengerAssignment) and is bought flat by shipped fix-it repairs, which is why it stays flat -- making it rated would make purchaseUnits throw for every caller that holds no quantity and would re-price those repairs. This row prices the hall FIXTURE at a landing, which section D553 made per-floor data (FloorConfig.landingCallType). WHAT READS IT TODAY, stated rather than left to be discovered: packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.ts#scheduleBoundsOf, through campaign/parse.ts, whose ceiling, cheapest positive step and affordable-purchase count all move because this row exists. WHAT DOES NOT: a purchase. The viewer refuses a building declaring landingCallType under the code landing-call-type-not-playable until GitHub issue #534's list is done (section D553 clause 9), so no shipped surface spends this rate yet, and that is the honest boundary of stage 2 rather than a dead seam nobody noticed.

changes.name: Pressurise the cabins
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #444. A flat equipment row, which is what this issue's own body asks for and what the schedule already grants; #478's magnitude term is not needed and its block on this issue was mis-applied. MEASURED: nothing. No shipped list prices this change, because it did not exist before #444, so there is no agreed figure to keep and no disagreement to record — unlike every other row in this file. CHOSEN: 11 units and 2 nights. 11 sits between door-sensors (9 u, 1 night) and destination-panels (13 u, 2 nights), which is where the ladder puts it by kind: it is a fitting on kit the building already has — a pressure vessel and a bleed valve on an existing cabin — rather than a new machine or a new shaft, so it is above a sensor and below a landing-panel refit. 2 nights matches destination-panels, on the reasoning that a car is out of service while its cabin is worked on. Both figures are game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). WHAT IT BUYS, and the reason it is not a dominant buy: it lifts the air-pressure descent cap in data/elevator-specs.json, which only binds a bank whose travel is above airPressure.appliesAboveTravelM and whose cars are rated faster than airPressure.descentCapMps. On every shipped building as built it buys exactly zero seconds, and the loader says so (pressurisation-buys-nothing). It becomes worth 11 units only after the player has bought speed the shaft cannot spend going down — which is the decision #444 exists to create.

changes.name: Fit regenerative drives
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #431, DECISIONS.md § D539. APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. A flat equipment row, which is what the issue's own body asks for. MEASURED: nothing. No shipped list prices this change, because it did not exist before #431, so there is no agreed figure to keep. CHOSEN: 12 units and 2 nights. 12 sits between cabin-pressurisation (11 u) and destination-panels (13 u): it is a drive and inverter retrofit on machines the building already has, which is more than a fitting on an existing cabin and less than a landing-panel refit, and well under machines-4mps (14 u, building tier), which is new machines. 2 nights matches cabin-pressurisation, on the reasoning that a car is out of service while its drive is changed. Both figures are game feel, and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). WHAT IT BUYS, and the reason it is a decision rather than a dominant buy: energy only. It moves energyKJ, workPerServedLegKJ and the fifth goal's verdict and never a leg (§ D539), and how much it moves them depends on how much of a building's travel overhauls. Measured on a 28-run probe under collective at § D468's seeds, the whole-run saving is 6-14 % at midtown-office, 13-21 % at chancery-house and secure-tower, 24-34 % at crown-hotel, st-jude-hospital and mixed-use-high-rise, and 31-43 % at garden-apartments — against the 20-40 % band elevator-specs.json's regenerativeDrive block cites.

changes.name: Rebalance the counterweights
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #431, DECISIONS.md § D539. APPROVED AS DRAFTED by the product owner on 2026-09-11. A flat equipment row. MEASURED: nothing; no shipped list prices it. CHOSEN: 3 units and 1 night. Adding or removing filler weights in a counterweight frame is docs/38 § 2.1's own description of the equipment tier — a setting on kit already installed — so it sits with the cheap end of that tier, between door-dwell (2 u) and faster-doors (4 u). 1 night because a car is taken out of service to be re-weighed. Both figures are game feel and the owner's. WHAT IT BUYS: energy only, like regenerative-drive. The ratio may be set anywhere in the cited 0.4-0.5 band (core config/schema.ts BANK_ENERGY_TUNABLES), and whether its best setting differs by traffic pattern is measured by benchmark/counterweightOptimum.ts rather than assumed; if it does not, the row is a dial that changes a number and not a decision, and the study says so. It does not: every measured optimum lies below 0.4, so the rebalance always pays, and the product owner kept the row as a purchase, as drafted, on 2026-09-11 (DECISIONS.md § D539).

changes.name: Move a floor
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #422. The elevation control: no row priced this before, because no `FixitPatch` field could move a floor at all until this issue gave it one (`fixit/types.ts#BuildingPatch.floors`). MEASURED: nothing about the figure, exactly as cabin-pressurisation's and rope-upgrade's notes say of themselves — no shipped repair or shipped list has ever priced a floor's own position moving, so there is no agreed figure to keep and no disagreement to record. DERIVED: the ceiling, on rope-upgrade's own precedent. docs/35 s 10.2 caps a fix-a-building case's budget at 16 u, and a row priced above that would be a seam no case could ever buy — the same dead-seam shape rope-upgrade's note measured at 20 u before it was moved to 16. So this row may not exceed 16 u either, and CHOSEN below stays under it with headroom for the case's own diagnosed repair. CHOSEN: 10 u and 3 nights. A floor's slab, the landing it opens onto and everything above it re-set to a new elevation is a fabric job on the shaft rather than a fitting on kit the building already has — docs/38 s 2.1's own line between the equipment and building tiers — so it sits with faster-machines (10 u, 2 nights, a machine swap) rather than with rezone-bank (6 u, a controller and a landing sign). 3 nights because more of the shaft is disturbed than a machine swap touches, and less than move-a-tenant's 4, which is a lease matter rather than a structural one. Both figures are game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). WHAT IT BUYS: only the building's topmost floor is offered a control (fixit/run.ts#topFloorRaiseCeilingOf), because raising it is the one move that can never break heightM's strict-increasing-with-index rule — every other floor is untouched. It changes travel time to and from that floor and, on a building already close to elevator-specs.json's airPressure.appliesAboveTravelM, can move a bank across that threshold; on a shaft near a fitted rope's maxSingleTravelM it can refuse the building outright, exactly as ropeClass already can, which is the constraint rather than a defect in this seam.

changes.name: The plan area a new shaft takes
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL -- GitHub issue #429 stage 2, DECISIONS.md section D630. AWAITING THE PRODUCT OWNER'S SIGN-OFF; nothing here is approved, and it carries exactly the status section D601's own shaftFootprint figures carry. WHAT THIS ROW PRICES: the plan area ONE NEW HOISTWAY permanently removes from every floor plate it passes through -- section D601 built that quantity (config/floorArea.ts#shaftPlanAreaM2, one car's footprint times the floors its bank's span reaches) and deliberately did NOT price it, because the product owner reserved the pricing as an economy decision rather than an engineering one. THE OWNER HAS SINCE RULED, on section D601 section 5's open question: area is priced in THIS schedule's existing units currency and not as a second budget axis, there is no Career income term, and it is charged in DISCRETE BANDS rather than at a flat rate per square metre. WHY NOT A RATE PER SQUARE METRE, which is the shape a reader will reach for first: section D601 section 5 measured that a shaft's area spans 49x across the shipped set (24.0 m2 for a car in ashgate's three-level car park against 1178.0 m2 for one more burj-class-reference shuttle), so the rate that keeps midtown-office's new-car at its agreed 34 u (0.238 u/m2) would price that shuttle at 280 u against a whole schedule of 587 u. That is not a tuning question; it is a different game, and the owner declined it. MEASURED: the distribution the bands are cut from, and nothing about the price. All 62 banks of the fourteen shipped buildings were resolved through the real loader and their one-shaft areas ranked: min 24.0, p25 176.0, median 240.0, p75 376.0, max 1178.0 m2. The THREE WIDEST GAPS BY RATIO in that ranking are 56.0->104.0 (1.86x), 640.0->850.0 (1.33x) and 376.0->464.0 (1.23x), and the four bands below are cut at 80, 400 and 800 m2 -- inside those three gaps and at round figures. The next-widest gap anywhere inside the 104-376 bulk is 1.10x, so a FIFTH band would have to be cut in air the distribution does not have; that is why there are four rather than the five a reader might expect, and it is a measurement rather than a preference. DERIVED: the ceiling, two ways. quantity.max is 3 because 3 is the highest band index any shipped building reaches, derived from data/buildings/ through the loader by pricing/shaftArea.test.ts rather than trusted from this file -- landing-panels' own precedent (section D620), so the schedule ceiling scenario/budget.ts derives stays true of every building the game ships. And the dearest band is set so that the dearest shaft in the game becomes the dearest single purchase on this schedule and nothing more: 34 u (new-car) + 24 u (band 3) = 58 u, just above fifth-car's shipped 54 u, which is today's dearest row. 58 is 20.7 percent of the 280 u the rejected linear rate produced, so 'well short' is an order-of-magnitude statement rather than a nudge. CHOSEN: 8 u per band, and a linear ladder over the band index (0, 8, 16, 24) rather than a curve. 8 is the step that lands the top of the ladder on the derived 24; the ladder is linear IN THE BAND INDEX and therefore strongly sublinear in area, which is the whole of the compression the owner asked for -- a shaft 49x the area of the cheapest costs 24 u more rather than 271 u more. Also chosen: that band 0 costs NOTHING, so the smallest shipped shafts (ashgate/carpark 24.0 m2, garden-apartments/main 33.0 m2, empire-state-class-reference/bank-g 56.0 m2) keep today's agreed 34 u exactly and a small building's price does not move at all. midtown-office/main is 142.8 m2 and lands in band 1, so the reference office's new car moves 34 -> 42 u; that is a shipped price moving, it is the point of the ruling rather than a side effect, and it is named here so nobody meets it as a surprise. THE BAND BOUNDARIES ARE NOT ON THIS ROW, and that is section D552's rule rather than an oversight: a rate carries one per-unit figure and its quantity and nothing that would bend the line, so rate.quantity.bands is refused by pricing/parse.ts. They are a pricing decision rather than a physical one, so they live in this document's own areaBands block beside the ladder, NOT in data/elevator-specs.json beside the footprints. WHAT READS IT TODAY, stated rather than left to be discovered: packages/viz/src/scenario/budget.ts#scheduleBoundsOf, whose ceiling moves from 587 to 611 u and re-derives every budget schema.max in data/campaign.json and data/engineering-briefs.json; and packages/viz/src/fixit/parse.ts#fixitContextOf, which resolves each shipped fix-it case's building and bank to a band so the eighteen new-shaft repairs are priced at their own building's banded figure rather than at a flat 34. WHAT DOES NOT: the campaign shop. campaign/economy.ts#shopTierPrice, campaign/career.ts and everyday/campaignModel.ts hold a CampaignCareer and a PriceSchedule and never a ResolvedBuilding, so the Shafts tier still quotes the unbanded 34 u and 54 u; threading a resolved building through those three modules is a refactor this lane did not take, and the honest boundary is said here rather than discovered later.

changes.name: Re-rope a shaft
changes.note: AGENT'S PROPOSAL — GitHub issue #433, DECISIONS.md § D583. AWAITING THE PRODUCT OWNER'S APPROVAL; neither figure has been approved. A flat building-tier row, which is what the issue's own body asks for ("Priced at the building tier of docs/38 § 2.1's schedule"). MEASURED: nothing. No shipped list prices re-roping a shaft, because nothing in the tree modelled a rope before #433, so there is no agreed figure to keep. CHOSEN: 16 units and 6 nights. Re-roping a hoistway is a fabric job on the shaft rather than a fitting on kit the building already has, which is docs/38 § 2.1's own line between the equipment and building tiers, and it is not a new shaft (new-car, 34 u). 6 nights sits between machines-gearless (5) and new-car (8), on the reasoning that the car is out of service while every fall is changed and the shaft is rebalanced. THE 16 IS CONSTRAINED FROM BOTH SIDES, and the owner should know by what before moving it. ABOVE: this file's own rule is that a tier's typicalUnits is the MEDIAN of that tier's prices, re-derived at load (packages/viz/src/pricing/parse.ts). The building tier held eleven prices and its median is 20; a twelfth above 20 moves it. This row was drafted at 28 first -- between machines-5mps (25 u) and larger-cars-21 (32 u), which is where the size of the job reads -- and the schedule then refused to load, saying the building tier declares a typical of 20 u while its own prices median at 25 u. So 20 is the dearest figure that leaves the building tier's typical where it is, and any higher price for this row is a deliberate move of that typical rather than a price change alone. THE SECOND CONSTRAINT took it from 20 to 16: docs/35 s 10.2 caps a fix-a-building case's budget at 16 u and fixit/engine.ts#toggleRepair refuses a repair a case cannot afford, so at 20 u no fix-a-building case could buy this row at all and the seam came back byte-identical on both arms -- which is what a dead seam looks like. 16 is the dearest figure that clears BOTH constraints. new-car (34 u) and fifth-car (54 u) stay deliberately unaffordable inside a case and are bought through a scenario's own ladder; a rope is priced to be buyable in both places, and the owner may decide it should not be. Both figures are game feel and the ladder's ordering is the product owner's (see this file's own header). ONE ROW AND NOT FOUR, and not a rate times a rise: § D552's magnitude seam could price a rope per metre of travel or per tier, and this row deliberately does neither, because schedule.test.ts forbids two rows covering one field and a per-metre rate would need a declared maximum quantity that nothing measures. Whether the dearer ropes should cost more than the cheaper ones is the owner's, and it is a second row rather than a correction to this one. WHAT IT BUYS, and why it is a decision rather than a dominant buy: energy, and a shaft that can be built at all. A lighter rope takes work out of every move (§ D583 publishes the measured figure rather than quoting the source's 15 %), and a rope's maxSingleTravelM is the only HARD ceiling on a hoistway's travel in this project — above it the configuration is refused, so on a tall enough shaft this row is not an optimisation but the purchase that makes the shaft legal. It moves energyKJ, workPerServedLegKJ and the fifth goal's verdict and never a leg, exactly as regenerative-drive does.

areaBands.$comment: AGENT'S PROPOSAL -- GitHub issue #429 stage 2, DECISIONS.md section D630, AWAITING THE PRODUCT OWNER'S SIGN-OFF. WHICH BAND a new hoistway falls into, by the plan area it permanently removes from the building (config/floorArea.ts#shaftPlanAreaM2: one car's footprint times the floors its bank's span reaches). The shaft-area row above charges rate.unitsPer for each band above the cheapest, so band 0 is free and band 3 costs 3 x 8 = 24 u. These are a PRICING decision and not a physical one, which is why they live here beside the ladder rather than in data/elevator-specs.json beside shaftFootprint: where the line between a cheap shaft and a dear one falls is game feel, exactly as 34 u is, and elevator-specs.json is CIBSE-cited reference data. The boundaries cannot sit on the row itself because section D552's ruling is linear only, no curves, and pricing/parse.ts accordingly refuses rate.quantity.bands. MEASURED, over all 62 banks of the fourteen shipped buildings through the real loader: the three widest gaps BY RATIO in the ranked one-shaft areas are 56.0->104.0 (1.86x), 640.0->850.0 (1.33x) and 376.0->464.0 (1.23x). The three boundaries below sit inside those three gaps, at round figures. A boundary is deliberately NOT placed at 200 m2, where seven shipped banks sit at exactly 200.0 and a 0.1 m2 authoring change would move all seven a whole price band. The table is contiguous from 0 with an open top, shaftFootprint's own rule, so every shaft lands in exactly one band.
